questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the academic level wasn't too low. That it was rather close to Copenhagen (didn't know what the state of the world with respect to COVID would be at the time of application). That the city had 'something to offer' in terms of history, culture and politics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a really tedious process. KU and HU have different semesters, so my preparations started way before HU even finished their second round of exams. It was quite frustrating since I felt I was always behind KU-wise but HU hadn't really started yet. For example, HU hadn't released the course catalog when I had to send in the preapproval. When the introduction began it was only a few weeks before the start of the lectures and questions usually arise in the process and not during the introduction lectures or when reading the (outdated) materials. I am surprised that it worked out in the end considering all the chaos.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: HUGS (student organization) had some introductory lectures on zoom, the faculty held an introduction day with a presentation and a dinner, and then the international coordinator was answering e-mails if my questions was understood.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I booked through an agency since I wasn't comfortable with booking with a private person before I arrived due to scams. I lived in Wedding in Village M which was close to the U-bahn and relatively central compared to some of those who lived in the dorms booked through HU. Their rent was almost half of mine but they had around and hour with public transport to Unter den Linde and I had 20 min.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are no on-campus accommodation for the campuses that are located centrally in the city. Those who I knew who have applied for accommodation through HU was living quite far outside of the city. Living in Berlin is expensive and there are a lot of scammers but it is not impossible to find a room in a shared flat (called WG).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Because of the preapproval process, I knew which courses I wanted to take. The process of registration for regular courses at my faculty was quite straightforward (on paper at least). 1. Find your courses on Agnes (their kunet-ish), keep an eye on the course descriptions where they will post a link to the Moodle (their Absalon-ish) and an enrollment key, 2. enroll on Moodle within some time limit. Officially you only have to register for the exam. The exam registration opens when the exam dates are released around 1,5 months before the exam period.
The process is different for seminars I believe but I don't know that process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An e-mail to reach the international coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It seems somewhat more relaxed than what I'm used to. The professors should tell you when you need to do something.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses is somewhat similar to KU. The exam period is crazy intense (I had 5 exams in 3 weeks and lectures in 2 of those weeks) but I was surprised by how high my grades were so I believe they might compensate a little bit. I didn't meet one HU student who did all of their exams in the first round. They split their exams so they did 2 in February and 3 in April.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Somewhat similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Applied Migration and Development Economics, Finance Theory, Economic Growth, The Theory of Labor Markets with Search Frictions, Introduction to Advanced Macroeconomic Analysis.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Theory of Labor Markets with Search Frictions: Really interesting topic and extremely nice professor (prof. Burda).  Introduction to Advanced Macroeconomic Analysis: It transfers as Business Cycles but it is really straightforward and easy points (prof. Weinke).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay Rundfunkbeitrag (German broadcasting fee). As with everything else, the registration process is in German but there exist some guides in English. I don't think the students living in dorms had to pay but if you live in private accommodation it is mandatory. It is around 18 euros per month per flat.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is cheap. Both in supermarkets and at restaurants.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't use any of them partly due to COVID.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some kind of sports and then the student organization HUGS also offered some guided tours and such.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Free guided tour! Not necessarily offered by the host university but it is definitely offered in all bigger cities in the world. Really good and interesting when moving to a new city. They offer different kinds of tours; historical, Cold war, foodies, etc. The thing is that you pay what you believe the guide deserves at the end of the tour so it is not totally free.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Berlin is relatively close to a lot of other cities for example Vienna, Prague, or Budapest.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. As long as you keep in mind that everything is a lot more formal.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everyone is on WhatsApp. That's where it happens.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really use to address the professors as 'professor [Last name]'.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is really not that different from the Danish 'culture'.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a huge load of practicalities with both HU, KU, and the German authorities (Anmeldung/Abmeldung/Rundfunkbeitrag, etc.). I spend so much time just uploading or filling out the right documents both before and also now after. It is never-ending and it is insanely frustrating. But I think that applies for everyone going on exchange. Sadly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exam period is crazy and since they don't release the exam dates it is close to impossible to plan ahead. The professors didn't really respect what was written in the introduction materials (lectures will end 3 weeks before the exam) so there wasn't any real exam period. My exams ended in late February so if you have to go back to start the semester at KU you have to devote some time to figure that out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I made it considering the number of hours I put into the courses. And also some of the perspectives you get from living in a city that relatively recently was reunited after years with different regimes and wars. Since Berlin - or maybe Germany on the whole - is an attractive place for people from all around the world, I met people from both Ukraine and Kashakstan who had a terrible start of 2022. It really puts things in perspective.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There are so many things that you need to get in order and really no one to help you. The workload from everywhere was immense. And never-ending. Not only in terms of studying but also with all this practical and formal stuff that you need to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
